extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR classifyMapGerms.lib (computational algebra / singular users computing standard bases of modules)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the classifyMapGerms.lib procedures modVStd and modVStd0: describes required argument types, what each procedure computes (standard bases of certain module sums with a maxideal(bound) term), return format, and a note about bound correction when an extra parameter is supplied. Includes worked examples showing typical calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd usage / parameter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage:

modVStd((M, N, I,bound, #); M is a submodule in A^r over the basering=:A, N ist a submodule in R^r over the subring R of the basering genrated by the entries of I
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the expected arguments and their mathematical meaning: M must be a submodule of A^r (A = basering), N must be a submodule in R^r where R is the subring of A generated by entries of I. Argument order is (M, N, I, bound, #). Example provided: construct I from polynomials, M=maxideal(1)*jacob(I), N=I*freemodule(2), then call modVStd(M,N,I,15).

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd compute purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute: a standard basis of A^r/M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r using modular version
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the mathematical object computed: a standard basis for the quotient/module sum A^r/(M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r) (written as 'a standard basis of A^r/M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r'). Implementation uses a modular algorithm. Example outputs (from the run) show returned polynomials/vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd return format
rubrics_metrics.description:
Return:

a list whose ist entry gives a list where each entry is a genrator of standard basis and second entry gives a list of generators after the reduced echelon form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return is a list: first entry = list of generators of the computed standard basis; second entry = list of generators after applying reduced echelon form. The documentation shows example returned lists (explicit polynomial vectors) illustrating the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd bound-correction behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description:
Note:

if # is not empty the bound is corrected by computing determinacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the optional '#' parameter is supplied (non-empty), the routine will adjust/correct the provided bound by computing determinacy; users should provide '#' to request automatic bound correction. Example calls in the doc illustrate typical bound values (e.g., 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd0 usage / parameter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage:

modVStd0((M, N, I,bound, #); M is a submodule in A^r over the basering=:A, N ist a submodule in R^r over the subring R of the basering genrated by the entries of I
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same argument expectations as modVStd: M in A^r, N in R^r with R generated by entries of I; argument order (M,N,I,bound,#). Example provided mirrors modVStd example but calls modVStd0(M,N,I,15).

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd0 compute purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute: a standard basis of M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r using the parallel modular version
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference vs modVStd: modVStd0 computes a standard basis of M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r (same mathematical target up to notation) but uses a parallel modular algorithm (intended to exploit parallelism). Users concerned with performance on multicore systems should prefer this when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd0 return format
rubrics_metrics.description:
Return:

a list whose ist entry gives a list where each entry is a genrator of standard basis and second entry gives a list of generators after the reduced echelon form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return format identical to modVStd: first list = generators of the standard basis; second list = generators after reduced echelon form. The documentation includes example outputs showing the same structure (polynomial/vector lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd0 bound-correction behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description:
Note:

if # is not empty the bound is corrected by computing determinacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with modVStd, supplying a non-empty '#' triggers automatic correction of the bound by determinacy computation. The doc's examples implicitly demonstrate use with/without such corrections.
